chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn Tha'labah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: One application of lime paste in the summer is better than ten in the winter.

key_terms.طَلْيَةٌ: Lime paste applied to the body for removing hair or sweat, used in ritual purity context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the number of lime paste applications in summer versus winter for ritual purity?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the practical wisdom of seasonal hygiene by stating that one application of lime paste (*tayy*) in summer is superior to ten in winter. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *fiqh al-waqi'* (jurisprudence of context), acknowledging that physiological factors like sweating and hair growth rates in the heat make summer applications more effective for maintaining ritual purity (*taharah*). It underscores the balance between religious obligation and natural human conditions in Shia legal theory.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hasan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin Sa’aba, from Ammar Al Sabaty who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Waxing in the summer is better than ten in the winter’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Ahmad ibn Tha’labah from ‘Ammar al-Sabatiy who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Applying (lime paste) once in summer is better than applying it ten times in winter.’”
